sources.snippet: III-B Least Frequently Used (LFU) LFU evicts items with the lowest access frequency when cache capacity is reached. This approach theoretically outperforms LRU for workloads with stable popularity distributions but suffers from "cache pollution" when access patterns evolve over time.

sources.title: Smart Caching System: LRU vs LFU Analysis - GitHub
sources.snippet: This project implements and compares two widely used cache replacement policies — Least Recently Used (LRU) and Least Frequently Used (LFU) — to study their behavior under different access patterns. The goal of this project is to understand how caching strategies impact system performance and why different policies are suitable for different workloads.

sources.title: No-Regret Mixing of LRU and LFU with Optimal Switching Cost
sources.snippet: Caching systems often rely on simple eviction policies such as Least Recently Used (LRU) and Least Frequently Used (LFU), which perform well in complementary request regimes. Recent policies such as LeCar and Cacheus combine LRU and LFU using ideas from the experts problem in online learning. Specifically, upon a miss, they randomize between the two eviction rules using probabilities derived from scores updated by tracking the history of past evictions.
